newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks likely to see firm floor.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Tokyo stocks likely to see firm floor.

text.p: Tokyo stocks are likely to be propped up this week by an upturn in economic indicators as shown in the Bank of Japan's "tankan" survey of corporate sentiment and May industrial production data released last week, brokers said.

The relief from worries about the economy could encourage market participants to test the key 21,000-point mark in the Nikkei 225 average, but strong profit-taking pressure at that level may limit the upside, the brokers said.
On Friday, the 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,523.75, down 61.79 points from its close a week earlier.
"An upturn in fundamentals seen in the 'tankan' and industrial output should support the market," said Kaoru Ichikawa, senior trader at Kokusai Securities Co Ltd.
"Worries about a slowdown in the economy had weighed down the key index. But they (the "tankan" and the May output) have soothed worries," he said.
But some brokers were concerned about a lack of stocks-buying and a recent decrease in trading volume.
"Unless volume grows, it would be difficult for the Nikkei 225 to test 21,000," said Kunihiro Hatae, general manager at Tokyo Securities Co Ltd.
On Friday, turnover shrank to 415 million shares on the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange from Thursday's 604 million shares.
Some brokers said the cautious stance of investors could be partly attributed to a mixed forecast in industrial output.
On Friday, the Trade Ministry said Japan's industrial production in May rose a preliminary 3.8 percent from the previous month on a seasonally adjusted basis.
But the ministry also forecast a 2.6 percent month-on-month fall for June and a 0.9 percent rise for July.
On Wednesday, the Bank of Japan's key tankan survey showed a surprising improvement in business sentiment.
Longer term, the Nikkei 225 average is expected to keep a firm tone, brokers said.

"The 'tankan' has improved incentives, proving that the market sees the status of the economy as the most important trading factor. We will be able to buy until the central bank moves to tighten its credit stance, as we have confirmed an upward trend in the economy," said a general manager at a securities house.

On Friday, Tokyo stocks closed lower after a brief rally prompted by the stronger-than-expected growth in industrial production in May fizzled out amid caution on the peak day for annual shareholders meetings, brokers said.
Brokers said a cautious mood prevailed in the market, as statistics show that the Nikkei 225 average usually closes down more than 100 points after the annual shareholders' meetings.
More than 2,300 Japanese firms held their annual meetings on Friday. Most of the meetings were held in the morning.
